author: Robert Carr
description: Chipotle-spiced chicken with browned sweet potatoes and peppers, lime-cilantro black beans, and a cool lime-yogurt sauce.
equipment: Two rimmed metal sheet pans for the oven method; one 18-by-13-inch vegetable pan plus a 12-inch stainless steel skillet with lid for the skillet option
Small saucepan, or microwave-safe bowl with vented cover, for beans
Measuring cups and spoons; fine grater
Knife and separate cutting boards for produce and raw chicken
Shallow refrigerator- and freezer-safe containers and separate sauce cups, for meal prep
Food processor with chopping blade, optional for larger batches of cilantro

groceryIngredients.note: Plain, unbrined chicken without added salt solution; about 680 g.
No-salt-added, 15 oz can; drain and rinse, yielding about 1 1/2 cups.
Large, for 1 tsp zest and 3 tbsp juice total.
Fresh, finely chopped; 2 tbsp sauce and 2 tbsp beans.
Pure ground chipotle, not a salted chili seasoning mix.
Not garlic salt; 1 tsp chicken and 1/4 tsp sauce.
Fine table salt; 3/8 tsp chicken, 1/8 tsp vegetables, and 1/8 tsp sauce. Do not substitute coarse salt by volume.

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, plain and unbrined
1 lb (454 g) sweet potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 3/4-inch cubes; peeling is optional
2 large red bell peppers, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 can (15 oz) no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed, about 1 1/2 cups
2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, divided: 1 tablespoon chicken and 1 1/2 tablespoons vegetables
2 large limes, for 1 teaspoon finely grated zest and 3 tablespoons juice, divided
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh cilantro, divided
1 1/4 teaspoons garlic powder, divided; not garlic salt
5/8 teaspoon fine table salt, divided: 3/8 teaspoon chicken, 1/8 teaspoon vegetables, and 1/8 teaspoon sauce
1/4 cup water for the beans, plus small amounts as needed
instructions: Heat a conventional oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C), with racks in the upper- and lower-middle positions. Prepare the washed vegetables, cilantro, and limes before handling chicken. Toss the sweet potatoes and peppers with 1 1/2 tablespoons oil and 1/8 teaspoon salt. Spread in one uncrowded layer on the vegetable pan. Roast on the upper rack for 30 to 35 minutes, tossing halfway through, until the potatoes are tender inside with browned edges. Check from 25 minutes and remove any pepper pieces that finish early.

While the vegetables roast, stir the yogurt, 1 tablespoon lime juice, 2 tablespoons cilantro, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/8 teaspoon salt in a clean bowl. Add 1 to 2 teaspoons water only if needed for a spoonable sauce. Refrigerate and keep the sauce and its utensils separate from raw chicken.

For skillet chicken, use the alternative in the notes instead of this roasting step. Otherwise, pat the chicken dry; do not rinse. Divide into four roughly equal portions and gently pound thick sections between sheets of plastic wrap to an even 3/4-inch thickness. Coat with 1 tablespoon oil, the chipotle, paprika, oregano, black pepper, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 3/8 teaspoon salt, and the lime zest. Space on the second rimmed pan. Put it on the lower rack after the vegetables have had about a 10-minute head start. Roast for about 18 to 24 minutes, checking from 15 minutes. Remove each piece when its thickest part reaches 165 degrees F (74 degrees C), then rest on a clean plate for 5 minutes. Wash hands and clean surfaces and utensils after handling raw chicken.

While the chicken cooks, combine the drained beans, 1/4 cup water, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon cumin in a small saucepan. Simmer gently for 4 to 6 minutes until hot, stirring occasionally; add a splash of water if dry. Alternatively, microwave in a covered, vented microwave-safe bowl in 60-second intervals, stirring until steaming throughout. Off the heat, stir in 1 tablespoon lime juice and the remaining 2 tablespoons cilantro.

Drizzle the remaining 1 tablespoon lime juice over the rested chicken. Divide the chicken, roasted vegetables, and beans equally among four plates and add one quarter of the sauce to each. Remove each component as it becomes ready rather than overcooking it while waiting. For meal prep, begin chilling promptly and keep the sauce in separate refrigerated cups.
notes: Allow about 55 minutes overall and 20 to 25 minutes of hands-on work with oven chicken. The skillet alternative needs more active attention and may add 5 to 10 minutes. The beans, sauce, and chicken preparation overlap the vegetable roasting. Cut the potatoes evenly and leave space between pieces; doubling the recipe needs additional pan space or separate batches, not a deeper pile of food.

Stainless-steel chicken option: Keep the oven method for the vegetables and replace only the chicken roasting step. Pat and pound the chicken to the same 3/4-inch thickness and apply the same dry seasonings and citrus zest, but put the chicken's measured 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet rather than on the meat. Preheat a 12-inch stainless skillet, such as All-Clad D5, over medium heat; add 1 1/2 teaspoons oil for each of two uncrowded batches. When the oil shimmers without smoking, add two portions and leave them undisturbed for about 3 to 4 minutes, until they release with a gentle nudge. Turn, reduce to medium-low, and cook about 4 to 7 minutes more, checking from 7 minutes total and continuing until every thickest part reaches 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). If spices darken before the center is done, lower the heat and add 1 tablespoon water, then cover briefly to finish. Do not force stuck chicken loose or cook until the spices turn black. Repeat with the remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons oil, resting each finished portion for 5 minutes on a clean plate, then add the finishing citrus as directed. Allow about 20 to 30 minutes for both batches and resting; begin while the vegetables roast. This is an alternative, not an extra sear after roasting, and uses no additional oil.

Chipotle supplies both smoke and heat. For a mild version, replace half the chipotle with an equal amount of smoked paprika. For more heat, increase chipotle to 3/4 teaspoon for the batch. The sweet potatoes and yogurt balance the chile; no honey, cheese, or bottled dressing is needed. Taste a bite of chicken, beans, vegetables, and sauce together before adding seasoning.

Use no-salt-added beans, plain unbrined chicken, and pure spices. The measured salt and oil cover the whole meal. Coarse or kosher salt is not interchangeable with fine table salt by volume. Plain nonfat yogurt also works. The sauce contains milk.

Meal prep: Divide cooked food promptly among shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 degrees F. Keep the refrigerator at 40 degrees F or below. Use refrigerated portions within 3 to 4 days; freeze later portions promptly after chilling rather than waiting until the end of that window. Label and freeze at 0 degrees F or below, aiming to use within 2 months for quality. Do not cool a large batch on the counter.

Store sauce separately at 40 degrees F or below and use within 3 to 4 days, or sooner if the yogurt label requires it. Freeze the chicken, beans, and vegetables without sauce; make a fresh small batch of sauce for later freezer meals. Yogurt may separate if frozen, and reheated vegetables will be softer than freshly roasted ones.

Reheating: Thaw one frozen portion overnight in the refrigerator. Add 1 to 2 tablespoons water, cover with a microwave-safe vented lid, and heat at medium to medium-high power in 60-second intervals, stirring or turning between intervals. Use shorter intervals near the end. After a 1-minute stand, check several spots with a thermometer and continue until all hot components reach 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Reheat only the portion being eaten and serve promptly. Remove the sauce cup before heating and add the cold sauce afterward.

Frozen vegetables: Plain frozen sweet potato cubes and pepper pieces can replace the fresh vegetables by weight. Follow their package cooking instructions; cook separately when their timing differs and expect a softer result. Avoid seasoned or sauced bags and retain the same measured oil and salt. Frozen sweet potato fries are not an equivalent substitution.

Optional food-processor prep: For several batches, pulse clean, thoroughly dry cilantro with the chopping blade, then measure the chopped amount and divide it between sauce and beans. A 14-cup Cuisinart DFP-14BCNY is optional; for a single batch, a knife and spoon are simpler. Keep the sweet potatoes in 3/4-inch cubes and peppers in 1-inch pieces cut by hand: the supplied slicing/shredding discs do not dice them, and thin slices would need different roasting times. Stir the small yogurt sauce by hand and prepare all produce before handling raw chicken.
title: Chipotle-Lime Chicken with Sweet Potatoes and Black Beans
